issue: Factual/lexical error: lontong is made from BERAS (uncooked rice), not 'nasi' (cooked rice). 'Dibuat dari nasi' teaches the wrong word in exactly the beras/nasi/padi distinction learners must master.

fix.target: Lontong dibuat dari beras yang dimasak di dalam daun pisang.
fix.english: Lontong is made from rice cooked inside a banana leaf.
fix.grammar: Beras = uncooked rice, nasi = cooked rice on the plate — lontong starts from beras.

issue: Pragmatics: warung staff never say 'Soto Anda' — 'Anda' is stiff signage/call-center language, and 'your soto' is an English possessive calque. The counter formula is just 'Nasinya dicampur atau dipisah, Pak?'

fix.english: Would you like the rice mixed in or separate, sir?
fix.grammar: Soto question at the counter: dicampur (rice in the bowl) atau dipisah (rice on the side)?

issue: Register: 'mengumpulkan uang bersama' is committee-report prose no one says across a table; the tip itself admits the real word is 'patungan'. Q4 should model patungan directly instead of tipping around it.

fix.target: Kemarin kami patungan untuk makan malam perpisahan tim.
fix.english: Yesterday we chipped in together for the team's farewell dinner.
fix.grammar: Patungan = pool money / chip in — the everyday word: patungan, yuk! = let's split it!

issue: Bureaucratese calque: 'melakukan video call' wraps the loanword in the empty formal verb melakukan ('conduct a video call'). Card id-2503's own tip says video call works as a verb as-is — this card contradicts it.

fix.target: Kami video call dengan tim Jakarta setiap Senin pagi.
fix.english: We video-call the Jakarta team every Monday morning.
fix.grammar: Video call is its own verb — no melakukan needed: kami video call setiap Senin.

issue: Texture-word precision: overgrilled meat is 'alot' (tough, chewy, fights back), not generic 'keras'. Alot is the exact word every satay eater uses and the deck never teaches it.

fix.target: Sate yang dibakar terlalu lama jadi alot dan kering.
fix.english: Satay that is grilled too long turns tough and dry.
fix.grammar: Alot = tough, chewy meat — the word for overcooked satay or cheap beef.

issue: Cooking authenticity: chicken headed for the grill is 'diungkep' (simmered in the spice paste), not plain 'direbus'. Home cooks and warung talk both use ungkep; direbus reads like boiling it in plain water.

fix.target: Sebelum dibakar, ayamnya diungkep dulu supaya bumbunya meresap.
fix.english: Before being grilled, the chicken is simmered in spices first so the seasoning soaks in.
fix.grammar: Diungkep = simmered in the spice paste before frying/grilling — the step direbus doesn't capture.

issue: Calque: 'mulut terasa terbakar' mirrors English 'mouth on fire'. The Indonesian word is 'kepedasan' (overwhelmed by spice) — a high-value ke-...-an form the node should be teaching here.

fix.target: Minum es teh manis membantu kalau kamu kepedasan.
fix.english: Drinking sweet iced tea helps when the spiciness is too much for you.
fix.grammar: Ke-...-an = overcome by: kepedasan = too spicy to handle, kepanasan = overheated.

issue: Collocation: alarms are 'dipasang' or 'disetel', not 'diatur'. 'Mengatur alarm' reads like managing alarm policy; everyone says pasang alarm.

fix.target: Setiap malam dia memasang alarm di HP sebelum tidur.
fix.english: Every night she sets the alarm on her phone before sleeping.
fix.grammar: Setting an alarm is pasang (or setel): pasang alarm jam lima = set a 5 a.m. alarm.

issue: Register: 'potongan harga' is ad-copy/formal; in app-and-shopping talk everyone says 'diskon' — which the deck itself already models (id-0210, id-1412). Casual Q4 sentence should match.

fix.target: Aplikasi belanja itu sering memberi diskon besar.
fix.english: That shopping app often gives big discounts.
fix.grammar: Diskon is the everyday word; potongan harga is what the poster says.

issue: Minor: for bakso the springy thing is the ball itself — 'baksonya kenyal'; 'dagingnya kenyal' reads as the meat filling being chewy. Kuah bening + kenyal pairing is otherwise perfect.

fix.target: Bakso di sini kuahnya bening dan baksonya kenyal.
fix.english: The bakso here has clear broth and springy meatballs.
fix.grammar: Kenyal = springy-bouncy — the prized bakso texture; lembek bakso is a failed bakso.

issue: Gloss: 'Fried catfish pecel' mistranslates the dish — pecel lele is not pecel-with-catfish; it is fried catfish served with sambal. Target sentence itself is fine.

fix.target: Pecel lele biasanya dijual di tenda kaki lima waktu malam.
fix.english: Pecel lele — fried catfish with sambal — is usually sold at roadside tents at night.
fix.grammar: Kaki lima = street vendors, named after the five-foot walkway (kaki lima) they occupy.

issue: Minor: 'traktir' is a colloquial (bare-root) verb modeled with no tip — the one card teaching this essential treating-culture word should gloss it. Q4 placement is fine.

fix.target: Kali ini saya yang bayar, kamu sudah traktir minggu lalu.
fix.english: This time I'm paying — you already treated last week.
fix.grammar: Traktir = treat someone (pay for them): aku traktir, ya = my treat.

issue: Minor spelling: KBBI standard is 'petai'; 'pete' is the colloquial spelling. Deck policy elsewhere models the standard form (cf. prangko). Doyan tip is good.

fix.target: Saya kurang suka petai, tapi suami saya doyan sekali.
fix.english: I don't much like stink beans, but my husband loves them.
fix.grammar: Doyan = really into a food (casual): doyan pedas = loves spicy food.

issue: Minor translationese: 'aplikasi pesan' is a label calqued from 'messaging app'; in speech it's 'aplikasi chat' (or just the app's name).

fix.target: Nenek belajar memakai aplikasi chat supaya bisa membalas cucunya.
fix.english: Grandma is learning to use a chat app so she can reply to her grandchildren.
fix.grammar: Chat is used as-is: aplikasi chat, chat saya belum dibalas = my message hasn't been replied to.

issue: Minor: 'dari luar toko resmi' is ambiguous ('official shop'); the referent is the app store — 'toko aplikasi resmi'.

fix.target: Jangan mengunduh aplikasi dari luar toko aplikasi resmi, itu berbahaya.
fix.english: Don't download apps from outside the official app store; that's dangerous.
